label: Town of Hartford
header:
# Town of Hartford municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 10; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists Hartford's seven selectboard members as Ashley Andreas, Miranda Dupre, Mike Eigenbrode, Mary Erdei, Tim Fariel, Ida Griesemer (Chair), and Erik Krauss.

Town of Hartford, Certificate of Results, Annual Town Meeting, March 3, 2026 (hartford-vt.org): the certified 2026 results re-elect Ashley Andreas (821) and Tim Fariel (828) to two-year seats over Janet Sharkey Potter (638), and Mike Eigenbrode (1,005) to a three-year seat.
Town of Hartford, Official Ballot Results, Annual Town Meeting, March 4, 2025 (hartford-vt.org): the official 2025 results elect Mary Erdei (1,191) and Miranda Dupre (807) and Erik Krauss (1,068).
Charter of the Town of Hartford, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 123A (official text, Vermont General Assembly): section 202(e)(1) fixes a seven-member elected selectboard.

Town of Hartford, Official Ballot Results, Annual Town Meeting, March 4, 2025 (hartford-vt.org): Chuck Wooster was elected Town Moderator for three years on March 4, 2025, with 1,416 votes; the seat did not stand in 2026.
Charter of the Town of Hartford, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 123A (official text, Vermont General Assembly): section 202(e)(2) makes one moderator elective on a three-year term.
Town of Hartford, Certificate of Results, Annual Town Meeting, March 3, 2026 (hartford-vt.org): Joe Major was re-elected Town Treasurer for three years on March 3, 2026, with 1,189 votes.
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Joseph Major as Hartford town treasurer.

Charter of the Town of Hartford, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 123A (official text, Vermont General Assembly): section 202(e)(3) makes a town treasurer elective on a three-year term. The holder is the sitting Windsor-district state senator; his existing person record is reused.

Charter of the Town of Hartford, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 123A (official text, Vermont General Assembly): the charter provides that the Town Clerk is appointed by and serves at the pleasure of the Selectboard.
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Lisa O'Neil as Hartford town clerk.
Town of Hartford, Certificate of Results, Annual Town Meeting, March 3, 2026 (hartford-vt.org): the 2026 certificate of results is recorded and signed by Lisa O'Neil as Town Clerk.
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen justices of the peace for Hartford.
Charter of the Town of Hartford, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 123A (official text, Vermont General Assembly): section 202(g) fixes fifteen justices of the peace for Hartford.

jp_election.name: Town of Hartford Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): the SOS listing names the fifteen Hartford winners of the November 5, 2024 justice of the peace election; the first-listed, Rebecca White, is the sitting Windsor-district state senator and her existing person record is reused. No lister post: the charter's contracted assessor performs the listers' functions. No delinquent-tax-collector post: the Town Manager holds the duties (ch. 123A section 203(c)). No West Hartford Library trustee post: its trustees are town-elected on five-year terms but no official source fixes the board's size (verified elected: Karen Powell and Mary Smith, 2025; Torrelee F. 'Fisher-Sass' Sass, 2026).
